documents.title: Doc 80 - Infringement - Car 12 - Unsafe release
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 12 - Unsafe release

details.fact: Car 12 was released in an unsafe manner into the path of Car 43.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.6.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty. (5 seconds added to elapsed Race time).
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 12 (Kimi Antonelli), team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 12 was released in an unsafe manner when Car 43 was approaching in the fast lane. While Car 12 was entitled to travel down the pit lane in parallel to cars in the fast lane, in this instance, Car 12 momentarily lost control on the slippery surface and had to take steps to avoid a collision and that resulted in a potentially unsafe situation. The team acknowledged that this release could have been handled better and in a safer manner. We impose a 5 second time penalty.

documents.title: Doc 79 - Infringement - Car 16 - Causing a collision
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 16 - Causing a collision

details.fact: Car 16 made contact with Car 30 in turn 12.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty. (5 seconds added to elapsed Race time).
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 16 (Charles Leclerc), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 16 made contact with Car 30 at turn 12. While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later. Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision. The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence. While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence. In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (ie minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5 second time penalty as opposed to a 10 second time penalty.

documents.title: Doc 78 - Infringement - Car 87 - Unsafe release
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 87 - Unsafe release

details.fact: Car 87 was released in an unsafe manner into the path of Car 16.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.6.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty. (5 seconds added to elapsed Race time).
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 87 (Oliver Bearman), the driver of Car 16 (Charles Leclerc), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, and in-car video evidence. BEA was released from its pit stop into the path of LEC, which was already proceeding along the pit lane. As a result, LEC was forced to brake and take evasive action, being squeezed towards the pit wall on the right-hand side. The Stewards determined that BEA was released in an unsafe manner and therefore imposed a 5 second time penalty.

documents.title: Doc 71 - Infringement - Car 27 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 27 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 27 left the track and gained a lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Breaches of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 c) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: 10 second time penalty.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed in-car video evidence and determined that Car 27 left the track while attempting to overtake Car 43 at Turn 1 on the outside. Car 27 then rejoined the track ahead of Car 43. Car 43 was ahead at the apex of Turn 1 and had the right to the corner per the Driving Standards Guidelines. Car 27 gained a lasting advantage by leaving the track. We imposed a 10 second time penalty on Car 27.

documents.title: Doc 67 - Infringement - Car 23 - Rejoining the track unsafely
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 23 - Rejoining the track unsafely

details.fact: Car 23 rejoined the track in an unsafe manner.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty. 2 penalty points (total of 3 for the 12 month period).
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 23 left the track at Turn 2 and rejoined at Turn 3 in front of Car 10, which was forced to brake. Cars on track should not be forced to slow down to accommodate a car rejoining the track. We accordingly imposed a 5 second time penalty per the applicable guidelines.

documents.title: Doc 66 - Decision - Car 11 - Alleged failure to slow under yellow flags
documents.subject: Decision - Car 11 - Alleged failure to slow under yellow flags

details.fact: Car 11 alleged failure to slow for double yellow flags.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, and in-car video evidence. The double yellow flags were triggered following an incident involving Car 51 (CAM), who lost control at Turn 1 immediately ahead of Car 11 (PER). The Stewards noted that PER had very limited time to react, as he was already approaching Turn 1 and had commenced braking when the double yellow flags were activated. The telemetry showed that PER braked more than on comparable laps and carried a lower speed through Turns 2 and 3. Furthermore, the time taken to complete the marshalling sector in which the double yellow flags were displayed was discernibly longer than on comparable laps. Taking all these elements into account, the Stewards were satisfied that PER reacted appropriately to the double yellow flags and reduced his speed sufficiently in the circumstances. The Stewards therefore determined that no further action was necessary.

documents.title: Doc 65 - Decision - Car 44 - Alleged leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: Decision - Car 44 - Alleged leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 44 allegedly left the track at turn 5 and gained a lasting advantage.
details.infringement: Alleged breaches of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Appendix L, Chapter IV, Articles 2 c) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed in-car video evidence and determined that Car 44 was attempting an overtake on Car 87 at Turn 5. In defending the position, Car 87 moved to the right and Car 44 was pushed off the track to avoid a collision. Car 44 clearly had the momentum for the overtake and gained no advantage by going off the track. We also noted that the position was subsequently given back by Car 44. We therefore took no further action.

documents.title: Doc 40 - Infringement - Car 11 - Driving in an unsafe condition
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 11 - Driving in an unsafe condition

details.fact: Car 11 drove in an unsafe condition.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.6.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Competitor: Formal warning.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed in-car video evidence and determined that the driver of Car 11 threw a small plastic piece out of the car. The plastic piece was a cable organiser that typically attaches to the seat belt. It dislodged during the session and the driver threw it out as he was concerned that it would lodge itself somewhere else in the car and create a safety issue. While we appreciated the fact that it was a small, light piece of plastic that was unlikely to cause any damage to another car or injure another driver, throwing materials onto the track during a live session is not appropriate for obvious reasons. We therefore issue a formal warning to the competitor to avoid similar situations from arising in the future.

documents.title: Doc 25 - Infringement - Car 51 - Unnecessarily impeding of Car 16
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 51 - Unnecessarily impeding of Car 16

details.fact: Car 51 unnecessarily impeded Car 16 in turn 15.
details.infringement: Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Driver: Reprimand (Driving). This is the driver’s 1st reprimand of the season.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 51 (Rafael Camara), team representatives and reviewed video, team radio and in-car video evidence and determined that Car 51 was warned multiple times that Car 16 (LEC) was arriving on a fast lap. Yet, Car 51 was weaving and moving well into the racing line. Car 16 had to take evasive action to avoid a collision by moving to the right, with a significant amount of the car off the track. The situation that was created was clearly dangerous and Car 51 should have taken more care to avoid impeding Car 16. While the typical penalty for impeding in a Free Practice session is a warning, in this instance, we are of the view that a reprimand is warranted.
